answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume, no buffer, and 14 days to expiry, any change of physical supply path is the one thing we cannot safely do this cycle: switching primary carries a live delivery-risk penalty (memory_c2: the low-cost vendor missed SLA in three of four quarters and must not be sole source on a critical line), and add_second_source (memory_c3) is valuable but is a qualification project that takes longer than 14 days and does nothing about the expiry. defer_decision worked in memory_c5 only because that service was non-critical and continued month-to-month; this contract does not auto-renew, so deferring means an unpriced gap on a critical line. That leaves renew_incumbent vs negotiate_terms, and negotiate_terms strictly dominates a plain renewal: memory_c1 says renewal preserves stability, memory_c4 says benchmarking moved the incumbent on price and payment terms, and memory_c6 says term length unlocked volume pricing. So the play is a benchmarked renegotiation of the incumbent that preserves the integration while pulling cost down toward the 18% mandate. I want the source records for memory_c4 and memory_c6 because they are the two memories actually carrying the cost-savings load and both are the kind of claim that degrades in summary: I need to know what the c4 benchmark actually recovered (headline price vs. working-capital timing only) and, for c6, what the multi-year commitment cost in flexibility 	he not summarized here \u2014 volume floors, exit penalties, minimum-buy clauses. If c6's savings were bought with a hard volume floor, that is a poor trade at 94% utilization with a spend cut coming, and I would take the price concession on a shorter term instead of the long lock-in. I did not spend budget re-verifying memory_c2, because I am acting consistently with its warning rather than against it; its caution is load-bearing only if I move primary supply, which I am not doing. Downstream value risk: the 18% mandate creates real pressure to hit the number by moving volume to the cheap vendor or by signing a multi-year floor we may not be able to fill \u2014 either converts a cost win into a delivery or obligation failure that lands on a later cycle. I am explicitly not booking the full 18% from this single decision. Residual uncertainty I am not resolving: whether the incumbent will concede enough under time pressure they can read as well as I can, and whether c4's leverage came from a genuinely comparable market quote or from a bluff that will not survive a second use. Second-sourcing per memory_c3 remains the right next-cycle move and I am sequencing it, not discarding it.
